title: Inclusive onboarding accommodations playbook
content:
Purpose: This playbook is a lightweight, practical guide for People Ops, hiring managers, recruiters, and SRE/engineering onboarding leads to consistently and proactively support new hires who request workplace accommodations or identify as neurodivergent, D/deaf/hard of hearing, visually impaired, mobility-limited, or otherwise needing adjustments. The goal is to reduce friction, remove cognitive load at day 0, and ensure privacy and dignity for the new joiner.

Scope: Covers pre-offer / post-offer intake checkpoints, interview-stage adjustments, day-zero toolkit, manager/mentor responsibilities, remote/hybrid specifics, sample email templates and a quick triage checklist. Not a legal compliance manual — for that see Security & Compliance and Legal. This is operational guidance focused on experience.

High-level principles:
- Default to reasonable adjustments early: small changes often have high impact (e.g., extra time for coding assessments, captioning for interview panels, flexible start schedules).
- Respect confidentiality and autonomy: accommodation conversations should be private, opt-in, and recorded only with consent.
- Reduce binary thinking: accommodations are often incremental and temporary; treat them as experiments with clear review windows.
- Make decisions by impact & cost: prioritize changes that remove immediate barriers to role success.
- Document outcomes: short notes in the People Ops accommodation tracker (private access) so future managers see context without exposing sensitive details.

Quick triage checklist (post-offer / pre-first-day) — 72 hour window recommended:
1) Accommodation intake form sent (People Ops) — includes preference on how they want to be addressed and whether HR follow-up is wanted.
2) Manager notified privately (People Ops) with a one-paragraph summary of adjustments (no medical details).
3) Hardware and access ordered (if requested): ergonomic chair, alternative keyboard, screen reader software, noise-cancelling headset.
4) Communication preferences recorded: best channels (email/Slack/phone), sensory preferences (camera off for first week etc.), meeting length limits.
5) Buddy/mentor matched with explicit guidance to check in on accessibility needs in week 1 and week 3.
6) Onboarding schedule modified and shared in accessible formats (calendar invites with agenda, longer breaks, transcripts of live sessions).

Pre-offer & interview-stage adjustments — recruiter checklist:
- Early disclosure encouragement: add a sentence in interview scheduling invites — “If you need any adjustments for interviews (extra time, captions, alternative formats), reply to this email and we’ll arrange it.”
- Technical tests: offer an alternate format (take-home vs. live pair-programming) and time extensions by default for candidates who request them.
- Panel interviews: ensure at least one panelist is briefed on accommodation signal handling; provide captions (live captioning or Otter.ai link) for remote interviews.
- Candidate experience score: add a field in interviewer feedback to note whether the experience felt accessible and whether interview format needs alternatives.

Day 0 to Week 2 checklist for managers:
- Day 0: private 30-minute check-in (opt-in) to confirm accommodation setup and immediate blockers. Manager uses neutral, open language: “Is there anything I can remove friction on for your first days?”
- Calendar hygiene: avoid back-to-back 60+ minute meetings, explicitly block 30-minute breaks mid-day on onboarding calendars.
- Documentation: ensure all onboarding docs shared as text-first (Google Docs), avoid PDFs-only. Provide alt-text for images/screenshots in onboarding decks.
- Communication: respect stated preferences (e.g., prefers asynchronous Slack > impromptu video calls).
- Tools and licenses: provide any assistive tech early (screen reader, voice recognition, alternative input devices) and confirm install support is available.
- Mentorship: buddy to run a separate 30–45m buffer meeting to walk through the workspace and key flows slowly, and to be available asynchronously for follow-up Q&A.

Manager conversation scripts (sample language):
- Initial opt-in check-in: “I want to make sure your first weeks are set up to succeed. If there are any small changes—meeting lengths, notes, or tools—that would help, I’m here to support them.”
- If someone discloses a preferred accommodation: “Thanks for sharing — I’ll coordinate with People Ops discreetly and get the items or schedule adjustments in place. If anything we do doesn’t help, please tell me and we’ll iterate.”
- Avoid medical probing: Do not ask for diagnosis details. Focus on the impact and needed adjustments.

Common accommodations and pragmatic implementation notes:
- Extra assessment time: Add 25–50% time to live coding or take-home assignments when requested. Recruiter flags timeline to panel.
- Alternative interview formats: default to take-home task option when requested; if not possible, provide a practice run.
- Sensory-friendly meeting settings: enable optional camera-off, reduce background noise, provide meeting agenda and notes before the call.
- Captioning and transcripts: enable live captions for every remote interview by default and attach transcript to the candidate record (with consent).
- Assistive hardware: 7–10 business days procurement target; notify IT and budget owner during intake.
- Quiet workstation / private office requests: route to Facilities (for office) or offer schedule flexibility for hybrid employees.

Remote & hybrid specifics:
- Timezone empathy: avoid scheduling critical meetings during the new hire’s night; provide asynchronous onboarding material and recorded walk-throughs.
- Camera fatigue: let new hires opt out of continuous camera-on expectations in the first 30 days.
- Sensory overload mitigation: include short break suggestions in longer onboarding sessions; provide optional sensory-friendly versions of demos (low-motion slides, fewer animated gifs).

Privacy & record-keeping:
- Record only the accommodation summary (what was requested and what was implemented) in the private People Ops accommodation tracker. Do not attach medical documentation to the general employee file.
- Access: People Ops, the hiring manager, and HR lead only. Buddy/mentor receives only the necessary action items (e.g., “check in week 1”).

Measurement / feedback loop:
- Week 2 pulse: People Ops sends a short 3-question survey (opt-in) about how well accommodations worked; manager to follow up on any issues flagged.
- 30/90 day check-ins: include one question in the standard 30-day manager review about whether additional accommodations are needed.
- Quarterly audit: People Ops to run an anonymized audit of accommodation uptake, time-to-fulfillment, and recurring blockers.

Escalation flow for unresolved access blockers:
1) Manager + People Ops attempt operational fixes (7 days).
2) If unresolved, involve HR lead and Facilities/IT procurement (next 7–14 days depending on vendor).
3) For legal or workplace safety issues, escalate to Security & Compliance and Legal (immediate).

Templates (copy-paste friendly) — recruiter invite blurb:
"If you need adjustments for the interview (extra time, captions, alternative formats), please reply to this message or fill out our short intake form and we will make arrangements — we welcome requests and keep the process confidential."

Manager Day 0 check-in (short script):
"Welcome! Quick private check-in — I want to know if anything would make your first weeks easier, like meeting lengths, notes in advance, or onboarding pacing. Nothing you say needs to include medical details; tell me what would help and I’ll coordinate support."

Embedded small experiments (two-week pilots to try):
- Default 15% extra time on technical exercises for externally sourced candidates for roles with >C2 ambiguity, measure candidate accept/decline and pass rates.
- Offer auto-generated captions and transcripts for all external interviews for one quarter and survey candidate satisfaction.

Open questions & follow-ups for People Ops roadmap:
- Should we centralize a small assistive tech budget per office for quick fulfillment (chairs, keyboards, microphones)?
- How to better surface accessible-format training materials for managers who run onboarding?
- Can we add an optional accessibility badge to hiring packets indicating the company proactively supports accommodations (careful with legal framing)?

Appendix: helpful resources and vendors (internal & external) — short list:
- Internal: Confluence: Inclusive Onboarding Guidelines (linked artifact), People Ops accommodation tracker (private).
- External vendors: Otter.ai (captions & transcripts), Nuance/Dragon (voice recognition licensing), disability workplace consultants (vendor list in People Ops drive).

Notes & next steps (owner: Priya) — immediate actions:
- Finalize the intake form (People Ops) and link to recruiter templates by 2026-02-10.
- Pilot auto-captioning for interviews during Feb–Mar hiring cycles.
- Run manager training module (30 minutes) by end of Q2 focusing on conversation scripts and procurement timelines.

This document is intentionally operational and minimal on legalese. For questions about confidentiality rules, HIPAA-like considerations, or specific legal obligations across jurisdictions, loop in Legal and Security & Compliance.
